claims.text: The ten OrderTests tests report a test time well under a second (241 ms); the seven integration tests first start PostgreSQL and Redis containers, and the whole run takes many seconds more on the clock (about 19 s).
claims.source_hint: verified by execution on git archive stage-2 (scratchpad it-a/evidence-tc.txt)

claims.text: The test pyramid pictures a suite with many fast unit tests at the bottom, fewer integration tests above, and very few tests of the whole running system at the top.
Each level up the pyramid costs more to run and set up and can fail for more reasons.

At stage-2 the status rules are checked in OrderTests (MarkPaid, Ship, Cancel cases); OrdersApiTests has one status-refusal test, ShipOrder_StaffAndNewOrder_Returns409NotPaid (409, type .../problems/not-paid).

With the not-paid check deleted from Order.Ship(), Ship_NewOrder_Throws fails (No exception was thrown; test duration ~0.1 s) and ShipOrder_StaffAndNewOrder_Returns409NotPaid fails with Expected: Conflict, Actual: OK.
claims.source_hint: verified by execution on a copy of git archive stage-2 (scratchpad it-a/evidence-tc.txt)

claims.text: An integration test pays for its cost where risk sits where parts meet (query, mapping, foreign key, HTTP contract, who may call); a unit test where it sits in a rule, since a unit failure can only come from that class.
When an application mostly moves data between HTTP and the database with few rules, putting most tests at the integration level is a reasonable choice; the pyramid fits where rules live in code.
claims.source_hint: outline item 4; DECISIONS 2026-09-27 integration-testing (9) opposing view

claims.text: Ship_NewOrder_Throws creates a new order, asserts Ship throws OrderStatusException with Code "not-paid" and that Status stays "new"; it uses no database or container.
ExceptionHandlingMiddleware turns every OrderStatusException into 409 with problem type https://donhang.local/problems/ + ex.Code; the staff caller in the API test passes StaffOnly before Ship runs.
OrdersApiTests has no API test for already-shipped or already-cancelled refusals; OrderTests covers them (Cancel_ShippedOrder_Throws, Cancel_CancelledOrder_Throws).
ProductsController.List reads DonHangDbContext directly; its comment says the list "has no rule to apply, only a query to shape".
The pyramid describes a shape, not fixed percentages; the right mix depends on where a system's risks sit.
claims.source_hint: outline misconception 2; DECISIONS 2026-09-27 integration-testing (9) no fixed ratio

claims.text: The OrdersApiTests run starts its PostgreSQL and Redis containers (Testcontainers also starts its own helper container) before its tests.

Because the middleware turns every OrderStatusException into 409 the same way, one API test of that path is enough to show the HTTP side; DonHang.Tests runs every test in-process, with no test of the whole running system at stage-2.
